questions.qtext:
People tend to estimate the likelihood of an event’s occurrence according to its salience; that is, according to how strongly and how often it comes to their attention. By placement and headlines, newspapers emphasize stories about local crime over stories about crime elsewhere and about many other major events.

It can be concluded on the basis of the statements above that, if they are true, which of the following is most probably also true?

options.text: The language used in newspaper headlines about local crime is inflammatory and fails to respect the rights of suspects.
The press is the news medium that focuses people attention most strongly on local crimes.
Readers of local news in newspapers tend to overestimate the amount of crime in their own localities relative to the amount of crime in other places.
None of the events concerning other people that are reported in newspapers is so salient in people’s minds as their own personal experiences.

questions.solution:
It is given that newspapers’ coverage of local crimes is stronger than that of non-local crimes.
Nothing is said about frequency of coverage so, we can not assume anything about it. However, all else being equal, we can assume that people tend to think the local crimes outnumber non-local crimes.
questions.subject: single | Marks +2 / -0.66

questions.qtext: A and B are related to C. C’s father’s sister’s only sibling’s son is B. C’s mother’s mother in law’s only son’s only daughter is A. How is C related to A and B respectively?
questions.solution:
C’s father’s sister’s only sibling is C’s father himself. Hence, B is C’s brother.
C’s mother’s mother in law’s only son is C’s father.
Hence, A is C’s sister. As A is only daughter of C’s father, C must be son. Hence, C is A’s brother and B’s brother.

questions.qtext:
Read the passage carefully and choose the best answer to the given question, out of the four alternatives.

It is no doubt true that we cannot go through life without sorrow. There can be no sunshine without shade. We must not complain that roses have thorns, but rather be grateful that thorns bear flowers. Our existence here is so complex that we must expect much sorrow and suffering. Many people distress and torment themselves about the mystery of existence. But although a good man may at times be angry with the world, it is certain that no man was ever discontented with the world who did his duty in it.

The world is like a looking glass: if you smile, it smiles; if you frown, it frowns back. If you look at it through a red glass, all seems red and rosy; if through a smoked one, all dull and dingy. Always try then to look at the bright side of things; almost everything in the world has a bright side. There are some persons whose smile, the sound of whose voice, whose very presence seems like a ray of sunshine and brightens a whole room. Greet everybody with a bright smile, kind words, and a pleasant welcome. It is not enough to love those who are near and dear to us; we must show that we do so. While, however, we should be grateful and enjoy to the full the innumerable blessings of life, we cannot expect to have no sorrows or anxieties.

The title that best expresses the idea of the passage is:

options.text: Smile a day and keep the doctor away

questions.solution: The passage emphasizes looking at the bright side and maintaining a positive outlook. Hence, optimism is the central theme.

questions.qtext: A square sheet of paper has been folded and punched as shown in the question figure. You have to figure out from amongst the four answer figures, how it will appear when unfolded?
questions.solution:
• The sheet is folded (most likely twice), so total layers = 4
• There are 2 holes punched in the folded figure, when unfolded, each hole appears 4 times i.e. total 8 holes.
• One hole is near top-right, so after unfolding appears in all 4 corners symmetrically.
• Other hole is near bottom-left, so it also reflects symmetrically across folds near the centre of the paper.

So final figure must have :
• 8 holes
• Perfect symmetry (both horizontal and vertical)

questions.qtext: In the adjoining figure, if the centres of all the circles are joined by horizontal and vertical lines, then the number of squares that can be formed is
questions.solution:
We shall join the centres of all the circles by horizontal and vertical lines and then label the resulting figure as shown.

The simplest squares are ABED, BCFE, DEHG, EFIH, GHKJ and HILK i.e. 6 in numbers.
The squares composed of four simple squares are ACIG and DFLJ i.e. 2 in numbers.
Thus, 6 + 2 = 8 squares will be formed.

questions.qtext:
Below are given three statements, followed by four conclusions. You have to take given statements to be true even if they appear to be at variance with commonly known facts and then decide which of the conclusion logically follow(s) from the given statements.

Statements:
Some tablets are capsules
No capsule is a medicine
All medicines are syrups


Conclusions:
I. Some tablets are not medicines.
II. All medicines are not capsules.
III. Some syrups are medicines.
IV. Some syrups are not capsules.
questions.solution:
• Since some tablets are capsules and no capsule is a medicine, thus some tablets are not medicines.
• Since no capsule is a medicine, hence all medicines are not capsules.
• From the Venn diagram, some syrups are medicines.
• We know all medicines are syrups and no medicine is a capsule. Therefore, the portion of Syrups that is Medicines can never be Capsules. Hence, Some syrups are not capsules.

Thus, all conclusion logically follows from the given statements.
questions.subject: single | Marks +2 / -0.66
